- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply mean reversion to 10–15% of recent average.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; lag forecast by 1–2 days to align with sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending sideways, model tends to drift upward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per period until sentiment confirms direction.
